items.title: The two geometric fibre-count functions of a locally quasi-finite map agree and are bounded on quasi-compact sources
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a locally quasi-finite morphism f : X -> Y the lemma states (1) the number-of-geometrically-irreducible-components function n_{X/Y} of the two preceding chapter lemmas agrees with the number-of-geometrically-connected-components function (both denoted n_{X/Y}), and (2) if X is quasi-compact then n_{X/Y} attains a finite maximum. The retained proof is written: on geometric fibres of a locally quasi-finite map the fibres are discrete topological spaces (Morphisms, lemma locally-quasi-finite-fibres), where irreducible components and connected components coincide pointwise, giving the agreement; boundedness comes from the chapter's universally-bounded dictionary (Morphisms, lemmas characterize-universally-bounded and locally-quasi-finite-qc-source-universally-bounded): a quasi-compact source forces uniformly bounded geometric fibres, i.e. a finite maximum of the count function. Retained author proof at lines 21971-21978.
